text:
alex: Heads up — customer Acme reported p99 spikes from 180ms -> 1.8s on their production endpoint since this morning. They say it started after the 03:00 deploy.

maria: seeing a p99 jump on eu-west in the SLO dashboard, confirmed around 03:02-03:30. p95 up too but less dramatic.

oncall-bot: ALERT: endpoint /v1/generate p99 breach detected (eu-west) — 75m above baseline.

samir: any 503s or errors or just latency?

alex: mostly latency, occasional `502` when backlog hits 1000 reqs. No auth/billing flags.

jess: I pulled the deployment diff — we rolled model-routing change that favors the new 30B quantized variant for small seq lengths. Could be routing fallout.

maria: timeline: deploy(03:00) -> routing change -> spike starts ~03:02 -> autoscaler started adding workers but lagged.

support-bot: support ticket #2471 opened by Acme; they attached request IDs.

samir: I’m reproducing a sample request against eu-west with `curl` — p99 consistent. Adding header `X-Trace` to trace.

maria: checking KV cache hit rates — they dropped from 68% -> 12% for this workload pattern after the model swap.

alex: interesting — if prefix/KV cache warmed for old model, new model variant likely incompatible with cache keys, causing cache miss storm and longer decoding.

jess: that would explain autoscaler + cold KV causing batching to back up. We also raised max batch size in config which could worsen tail.

samir: logs show many requests hitting model-variant `redwood-30b-q4_1` and waiting on first token gen.

maria: preflight checklist for mitigation: 1) route traffic off new variant 2) enable circuit-breaker fallback to 13B quantized 3) set short-term soft rate limit for this customer 4) warm KV cache / revert batch size tweak.

alex: agree. Let's coordinate quick steps.

jess: I can flip routing policy to prefer `redwood-13b-q4` for the Acme customer and region within 2min. That should return to previous cache behavior.

samir: while jess flips, I'll enable circuit breaker fallback: set `fallback_model: redwood-7b-q4` for requests > 600ms latency OR when queue depth > 200.

maria: I'll patch autoscaler to be more aggressive for the next 10m and reduce max batch size from 128 -> 64 to reduce per-request queueing.

alex: support: can you message Acme that we detected a model routing regression, doing an expedited fallback to lower-latency variants and may throttle bursts briefly? Ask for most-recent request IDs. :thumbsup:

support-bot: message sent to Acme, included trace header guidance.

oncall-bot: ACTION LOG: routing rollback initiated by jess at 03:12, circuit-breaker enabled by samir at 03:13, autoscaler adjustment by maria at 03:14.

jess: routing flip done. Verified traffic now hitting `redwood-13b-q4`.

samir: circuit-breaker rule active. Falling back for affected requests. Queue depth dropped from 420 -> 90 within 90s.

maria: KV cache hit rate climbing back to 54% after routing shift, p99 trending down.

alex: monitoring — p95 ~120ms, p99 ~210ms now, within SLO for Acme.

support-bot: Acme replied: "Thanks — latency is back to normal, appreciate the quick response."

jess: follow-ups: 1) run a controlled canary re-roll of model routing with warmed caches and bridge rules 2) add preflight check that new model variant accepts cache keys or warms mapping 3) create a regression alert to detect cache-mismatch spikes.

maria: ops changes I'll make: add a guardrail that prevents enabling new routing variant cluster-wide until we observe KV cache compatibility metric >= 70% in a canary region; and add a temporary circuit-breaker threshold so queue depth > 150 triggers fallback, not 200.

samir: also recommend a short-term mitigation playbook snippet for oncall: 
```
Mitigation checklist (short):
- If p99 spike post-deploy: check model-variant routing changes
- Validate KV/prefix cache hit rate for that variant
- If hits drop > 50%: route to last-known-good variant
- Enable circuit-breaker fallback to smaller model for tail
- Reduce max batch size and increase autoscaler aggressiveness for 10m
- Inform customer and ask for traces
```

alex: I'll open an action item to bake this into the latency-playbook and link to rollout runbook. Also assign postmortem to jess+maria+samar for root cause and rollout improvements.

jess: noted. I'll add migrations to our model onboarding checklist: `cache-key-compat` test and a cold-start tail sim.

maria: will follow up with a dashboard panel for `cache_compatibility_ratio` and an alert when it drops > 40% relative to baseline.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — p99 reduced to SLO within 8 minutes.

alex: great work team. Quick retrospective notes: don't allow global routing flips without canary; add automated fallback policy per-customer tier; and add soft throttles for bursty enterprise tenants.

support-bot: Acme closed their support ticket with thumbs up.

(small follow-on) samir: one more thing — create a runbook snippet: `rollback-routing` CLI: `redwoodctl routing set --endpoint /v1/generate --variant redwood-13b-q4 --scope acme --region eu-west` — saves time next time.

jess: adding CLI snippet to playbook now. :white_check_mark:
